highlights.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
highlights.summary: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
body: Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms.

All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two.

highlights.title: Red Roses’ four-year record gone – but good for women’s rugby?
highlights.summary: November 12, 2022 - the date England's Red Roses last lost a Test match before suffering defeat to Canada in Toronto a week ago, four years on.
body: Between their galling 2022 Women's Rugby World Cup final defeat to New Zealand at Eden Park and last week, the Red Roses went 41 Tests unbeaten, winning 39 consecutive matches before a draw against Canada in Exeter last month.
England's dominance is even more stark when you take into account that before that 2022 defeat, they had gone on a 30-Test winning run between November 2019 and November 2022.
Before last week in Canada, therefore, England had won 70 of their previous 72 Test matches. Astonishing and remarkable in equal measure.

Some eight Six Nations titles have been won in a row, in near totally dominant fashion too between 2019 and 2026, while a third World Cup triumph to sit alongside 1994 and 2014 was finally clinched on home soil in 2025, after final defeats in 2017 and 2022.

highlights.summary: When it comes to finding big discounts on physical video games, Black Friday is the time to watch out for. This sale event usually doesn't start up until November, but Amazon's been sneaking in some offers before then for eager shoppers to check out.
body: Requiem's deal price is actually a return to the price we saw during Amazon's recent October Prime Day sale event, which marked a full $20 discount off its MSRP. In a similar position is Star Wars Zero Company, which is just pennies away from its Prime Day price at the retailer, saving you just over $10 compared to paying its full cost.

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is another that caught our eye - initially as part of the Square Enix sale that popped up at Amazon recently - that's also returned to its lowest price point at Amazon. Right now it's available for just $20, which is a steal in comparison to its launch price of $70. And with Final Fantasy VII Revelation coming out next year, this is a perfect time to play it if you haven't yet.

Another standout game on sale right now is Pragmata, which is also back down to its lowest point at the retailer. It did dip to $39.99 during the most recent October Prime Day sale at Amazon, but that was exclusive to Prime members. For everyday shoppers, this is still a nice discount to jump on for one of our favorite games of the year so far.

highlights.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
highlights.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

highlights.title: ‘Tangles’ Wins Grand Jury Prize at Animation Is Film Festival
highlights.summary: “Tangles” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival. Directed by Leah Nelson, the 2-D animated film follows a family impacted by their mother’s battle with dementia.
body: The jury said: “’Iron Boy’ is pure beauty from the medium we all love. Louis Clichy’s ‘Iron Boy’ was an easy stand-out thanks to its beautifully crafted water-color-like and Chinese ink-brush style visuals and how it told a story inspired by the director’s own memories of growing up in rural France. We also admired the way Clichy conveyed a world of emotions with his impressionistic visuals as well as his depiction of a young boy’s personal struggles with a physical handicap and the heartfelt portrayal of a strained father-and-son relationship which avoids sentimentality and the pitfalls of a traditional comic-of-age story.”
“Paper Trail,” directed by Don Hertzfeldt, won the Shorts Jury Grand Prize. The jury described the film as “unique and profoundly moving.”

The Shorts Special Jury Prize went to “Please,” directed by Anna Mantzaris. The jury called it “a wonderfully made, funny, and tender film that captures the absurdity and very human longing for connection.”

highlights.title: Microsoft shuts down its beloved maker space
highlights.summary: Microsoft is closing down The Garage, a set of popular maker spaces where employees worked on experimental projects and collaborated on surprising new apps and hardware during the company's annual hackathon events.
body: “We’re winding down The Garage program as a centralized function,” says Microsoft in an internal FAQ to employees, seen by Notepad. “We will continue to explore new ways to help employees build skills, collaborate across boundaries, and bring a hacker mindset to their work.” GeekWire first reported on The Garage’s closure.

The main Garage space was located at Microsoft’s Redmond, Washington, campus and served as the central hub for around 15 Garage locations across the US, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. Microsoft employees could use it to experiment with prototypes, build hardware, and even turn hobbies into full Microsoft products.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella regularly attended Garage hackathons, giving employees a chance to showcase their projects and attract the attention of senior executives. Many apps and services have emerged from The Garage over its 17-year history, including the AI-powered Seeing AI app that describes objects and text to people who are blind or have low vision. It was born out of a 2015 hackathon event and shipped 10 years ago.

highlights.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation. You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is
body: The Microsoft cofounder isn’t an AI doomer, but he says it’s still “the most dangerous weapon of all time.”

In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”

In interviews since, Gates has called AI “the most dangerous thing that humans have ever gone near,” and that AI “makes nuclear weapons look like nothing.” It is clear he does not think the current policy response from the White House, or the lack of coordinated efforts from the AI industry itself, is sufficient to combat this threat.

So I wanted to know: Is Bill Gates an AI doomer? I also had a series of questions downstream from what he’s been arguing about AI. How can we ever hope to control AI, and align it to humanity, if we can’t even agree on what it is and whether it’s conscious? How would you even technically construct a solution to alignment that could be enforced, not just for closed-source models but open-source ones, too?

highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering ’s Star Trek Universes Beyond set is drawing inspiration from across the sci-fi franchise’s 60 year history, including references to all of its shows and films.
body: "Sagas have emerged as an exceptional design tool for presenting story arcs from other universes because of their episodic nature," senior editor Matt Tabak told Polygon. "Each chapter of a Saga can focus on an individual story beat, so when you put them together, you get a great overview of an entire episode in only a few abilities."

All Good Things… is named after the TNG series finale. The machinations of the near omnipotent trickster Q cause Picard’s mind to jump between the show’s present day, the period just before the Enterprise's first mission in the series premiere, and 25 years in the future. In each timeline, the Enterprise encounters a temporal anomaly that could prevent life from evolving on Earth. Picard must synchronize all three versions of his ship to protect the timeline and prove to Q that humanity is worth preserving.

highlights.title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
highlights.summary: Last year, we reported on Red Viper, a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo's famously failed red-on-black "portable" 3D headset from the '90s.
body: Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy's four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color's readme files explain how the emulator's game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8x8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash, for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game.

The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements.

highlights.title: 1Password lets AI agents use your passwords without seeing them
highlights.summary: 1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords. The aptly named 1Password for Agents doesn't give bots free reign to access all of your connected accounts - you'll still need to grant approval for sign-in…
body: Just grant the agent access approval and it’ll sign into your accounts to complete tasks.

”Agents are starting to do real work on our behalf. The old model where you hand over a credential and hope for the best doesn’t work,” 1Password chief product officer Aashish Tripathi said in a press statement. “An agent should be able to do the job it’s been asked to do without getting permanent access to everything behind the account, and 1Password provides the trust layer that makes this possible across personal agent experiences.”

With this new system, an AI agent uses a unique digital key to verify its identity to 1Password when it reaches a sign-in form. The app then sends you a notification about which account credentials it needs, and why. If you choose to approve the request, 1Password will fill in the required login information instead of handing it to the agent. Approvals are granted on your own device to ensure you’re behind the permissions, making this a similar process to two-factor authentication. After the agent is signed in, it’ll continue with its task, without ever having actually seen your password.
points: 1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords.

highlights.title: Who was right about Man Utd tactics: Carrick or Fernandes?
highlights.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and head coach Michael Carrick disagreed over the team's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. So who was right?
body: Fernandes said United gave Como too much time and space in possession and blamed this on the staff's decision not to press man to man.
United have been attempting to press man to man at times this season, often with bad outcomes. You can see just how ill-suited the current group are for that approach here.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. "But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."
Fernandes is not wrong to say United gave Como a lot of space. The Italian side completed 600 passes, which is more than any other team in a game against United this season.

highlights.title: Universes Beyond Is About to Ruin the best Magic: The Gathering Set of the Year
highlights.summary: Being a Magic: The Gathering fan has become an intense hobby. While the beauty of Magic lies in its variety, as the game offers ample choice of formats and ways to play, the quick pace of new set releases has affected the Magic experience overall.
body: Reality Fracture is by far one of the best Magic sets to come out in 2026. It brought a long-running storyline to a close (even if it wasn’t very satisfying ), culminating in the death of Jace Beleren, one of the game’s most iconic characters. Moreover, in terms of the Limited format, Reality Fracture is surely the best set of the year. Limited play (Draft or Sealed) is one of the most common ways to experience a new Magic set, as you play only with cards from that set. Limited players have been singing the praises of Reality Fracture since its debut, but unfortunately that's ending soon, making way for a new Universes Beyond set: Star Trek.

Reality Fracture was released on Oct. 2, with prerelease events starting on Sept. 25. It's the sixth of seven Magic sets released in 2026 (eight if you count Mystery Booster Commander Edition ). Reality Fracture succeeds in translating flavor and story into interesting gameplay mechanics. The most notable element is the presence of the Jace planeswalker tokens created through the Empower Jace mechanic. These are available to all colors and have a big impact on the set's Limited gameplay, but that's not all that Reality Fracture has going on.

highlights.title: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
highlights.summary: Step one in convincing people to live with robots with cameras on their faces? Disguise them as cute home decor.
body: You've had a long day. You finally get home, fling the door open, plonk on the couch, and let out a big sigh. In the corner of your eye, you notice your mushroom lamp perk up. Its microphone must have heard you come in. Its head raises to reveal round, animated eyes, and a little diamond-shaped nose—which actually houses a camera.
It does a little jiggle because it sees you're back. Its name is Mori.

As you move around the space—maybe it's time to start cooking dinner—the little robot's face follows you, observing your movements and making soft sounds that are a cross between a bird and R2-D2. The day's stress catches up, and you need a moment to relax, so you head over to Mori, touch its head, and its eyes and camera-nose dip back inside its body. It goes back to being a lamp, except now it plays nature soundscapes so you can feel at ease.

That's the pitch from OKA, or One Kind Artifact, a new startup based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and Shenzhen, China, focusing on experimental technology. CEO Hua Wang tells WIRED he wants his company to create five experimental “Artifacts” over the course of OKA's lifetime. Mori is the first.
points: Step one in convincing people to live with robots with cameras on their faces?

highlights.title: Meta strikes deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot billionaire tax bill
highlights.summary: Chief executive agrees to remain in California for eight years even if state brings in one-off 5% wealth tax. Meta has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot a possible California wealth tax targeting billionaires.
body: The social media company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp revealed on Wednesday night that the arrangement would keep its chief executive living in California, where Meta’s headquarters are located.

Under the deal, Zuckerberg will receive new shares that could be sold to potentially foot a multibillion-dollar tax bill in the event that California passes a one-off billionaire tax. In return, he is committed to remain a resident of the state, or wherever Meta maintains its base, for eight years.
Californians will vote early next month on Proposition 40, a one-off 5% tax on the roughly 250 billionaires who live in the state.

Zuckerberg, worth $239bn (£180bn) according to Forbes, told Meta he was considering moving his primary residence elsewhere because Prop 40 could expose him to a massive tax liability, potentially forcing him to sell voting shares to pay it.

And these three prove that “survival game” can mean very different things and have completely different gameplay.
body: One is a co-op horror-comedy set in a coal mine, one is an open-world sandbox after a zombie apocalypse, and one sees you stranded alone on a 24-island archipelago after your ship mysteriously crashes. You can play all three games right now, with two of them having free demos as part of Steam Next Fest and one already fully released with a huge new content update for spooky season.

Three generations ago, the sky froze. Now, your coal mining town is perpetually covered in snow. You might think that would be the end of the mine, but nope, the state kept it open and is forcing miners to continue delving into its depths. That might sound a bit dystopian, but it’s a premise that Coal Duty mines for humor as well as coal.

It’s a co-op extraction game for between 1–5 players, and you play as a group of miners who must navigate the many dangers of the mine to survive and get out with the materials you gathered. Each run is procedurally generally, so you’ll need to work together with your teammates to figure out how to progress.

highlights.title: A financially comfortable friend has set up a GoFundMe for vet bills. Is this socially acceptable? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: Your friends may have had good intentions when making this ask, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But that needn’t dictate how you feel about it. A friend, who I believe is financially comfortable, set up a GoFundMe page to pay for vet bills for their sick dog while on holiday overseas.
body: The family appears to be financially comfortable; both adults have good jobs, own two cars, have all the latest gadgets like expensive bikes and sporting equipment, take an annual holiday overseas and domestic holidays throughout the year, and live in a big house in a well-to-do area.
Is it socially acceptable to ask for money publicly in these circumstances?

Eleanor says: I’ll never forget someone posting their household expenses as proof it’s hard to get by on two six-figure incomes. By the time they’d paid for holidays, two cars, private school fees, insurance, extracurriculars, the mortgage and savings, there was nothing left!

They really did think this was proof they weren’t well-off. I suppose in some sense they’re right. Once you use your money to secure your financial future and have a high quality of life, you don’t have a Scrooge McDuck pile left over.
points: Your friends may have had good intentions when making this ask, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.

body: Apple’s Mac Mini M4 has become a popular mini-yet-mighty desktop computer for running local agentic AI 24/7—so much so that it’s been out of stock for months. But with the introduction of the new Mac Mini M6, the older M4 is no longer as scarce (there was no M5 Mac Mini), and the base model (256-GB hard drive, 16-GB unified memory) is on sale for $649—$150 off MSRP and $250 cheaper than the M6.

It’s a good deal for a computer that is plenty powerful for most people, and some M4 Mac Mini configurations can even handle AI tasks. But—and it’s a big but—shoppers should be aware that the M4’s original base price was $599 when it launched in 2024. However, with Apple raising prices on hardware across the board this year, driven by chip and memory shortages, the M4 ended up costing $799. In comparison, the new M6 starts at $899.

Depending on how you look at it, it’s either a discount or a hard pill to swallow, knowing that it used to be much cheaper. If you’ve been eyeing a new Mac Mini and don’t need the better performance of the M6, you’re unlikely to get a lower price than this M4.

highlights.title: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary.
highlights.summary: Using an AI agent to shop for you is a strange experience. Tech companies have marketed them as personal assistants - the democratizing of labor that ordinarily would only be available to the rich and powerful.
body: AI agents are getting blocked left and right — but even when they work, it suggests a more annoying future for humans.

Meta, Google, OpenAI, and others have all introduced some version of agentic shopping tools that promise to make buying things even easier than it already is. Demos show AI agents that can seamlessly book flights and hotels, browse billions of products to find the right one, and secure tickets to sporting events on a human’s behalf. But as AI companies — and their users — are finding out, buying things requires that the other party is willing to sell them in the first place.

Even without hard blocks, agents’ access to retailers is spotty. For example, Muse, which I instructed to look for a specific face moisturizer, was caught in Target’s bot check one day but was able to get through the next. It suggested a listing from a grocery chain that doesn’t ship to my address when I searched for the best price on granola bars. When I asked for mattress recommendations under a certain price point, Muse was once again blocked by Target, despite being able to pull from the site just a few minutes prior.
points: Using an AI agent to shop for you is a strange experience.
Tech companies have marketed them as personal assistants - the democratizing of labor that ordinarily would only be available to the rich and powerful.
AI agents are getting blocked left and right — but even when they work, it suggests a more annoying future for humans.

highlights.title: Eiliko maker says it’s hiring an ‘independent security firm’ after Verge report on its insecure robots
highlights.summary: Eiliko, a cute robot charm you can hang on your bag with built-in AI conversations, turned out to be a security nightmare. It told owners that "your secrets are safe with me," but hackers could easily read complete transcripts of everything we told the toy, and that was just the beginning.
body: Now, the company is finally breaking its silence, though its response leaves something to be desired.

“We have confirmed the core issues identified in your reporting and are addressing each of them,” Energize Lab told The Verge in an unsigned statement from a generic email address, which it later told us is attributable to CTO Du Xiaoyu. The company says it will hire an independent security firm to fully review all of its systems, and has set up a dedicated security@energizelab.com contact email.
The company also claims that as of Wednesday, it has “closed all external access to our backend systems” and “disabled the interface that allowed a robot’s responses to be modified remotely.”

Energize Labs is also pledging to “no longer store conversation records or the user profiles generated from them,” and says it will delete the conversation records, user profiles, and “avatar images” it has already stored.
points: Eiliko, a cute robot charm you can hang on your bag with built-in AI conversations, turned out to be a security nightmare.

highlights.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
highlights.summary: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer. Sign up for our free newsletter here. Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner.
body: Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets.
Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.
